conviction_note: Q3's headline lines are already out (Rx Germany +56%, adj. EBITDA margin flat QoQ, ad-hoc and press release of 28 Sep 2026), so the move sits on the guide and on what the 28 Sep release left unsaid. The company's own numbers make the FY guide look conservative (+1.0). A soft German non-Rx market (-0.6), the new CEO's first call (-0.3) and a peak-capex cash line (-0.3) pull the other way, so the findings sum to -0.2. Against that sits a +33% run-up since 25 Sep and a record of fading results-day gaps (Q3'25 opened +4.7% and closed -3.3%; Q2'26 opened +5.2% and closed +2.1%, then fell -6.6% the next day). The 4.28% disclosed short is fuel on any raise. Net, p_up stays at 50 and the signed number is 0; abs_move is 6.5 because a guidance change is plausible.

findings.finding: The company's own numbers make the FY2026 guide look conservative. Rx Germany 9M is about EUR 545m (H1 348 + Q3 about 197 at +56% on Q3'25's 126). Against EUR 730-760m that implies Q4 Rx Germany of EUR 185-215m, +19% to +39% on Q4'25's 155m, while September ran at +51% against the bonus-introduction base. Likewise 16-18% group growth implies Q4 growth of only about 7-14% after about 20% in 9M. The 29 Oct release carries October data and a new CEO, so a third raise or an upper-end steer is a live guidance event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises by ad-hoc moved the stock hard: 15 Jun 2026 +17.4% and 28 Sep 2026 +12.7%. When the raise was already out, the results day faded: Q2'26 'upgraded guidance confirmed' gapped +5.2% and closed +2.1%, then fell -6.6% the next day. The first FY26 guide on 4 Mar 2026 brought -21.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Deutsche Bank (18 Sep) called the targets conservative, Berenberg and MPCM raised targets on 7 Oct, and the stock is up 33% since 25 Sep. What is not priced is a formal third raise. Had the market fully discounted one, the 4.28% short would be covering rather than flat, and the stock would not have spent 8-28 Oct range-bound at 70-78 after the 7 Oct spike. German trade press reads the same guide the other way: Venlo still expects a flattening curve and Q4 could come in weaker than Q3. So the market is split on this line.
findings.independence: Base figures come from separate primary documents: Q3'25 Rx Germany 126m in the Q3 2025 release (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/redcare-pharmacy-scaling-rx-and-strengthening-operating-cash-generation-with-adj-ebitda-margin-of-2-4-in-q3/6d05edba-eefa-48f1-a5c7-d4e9cfe8e44e_en) and FY25 Rx Germany 503m / revenue 2.94bn in the FY2025 release (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/redcare-pharmacy-strong-growth-in-2025-surpassing-eur-1bn-in-rx-revenue-adj-ebitda-up-72-yoy/4d756ba7-ebd1-4b54-8610-bcb06263b44d_en). The sell-side view is Deutsche Bank's 'Jahresziele erscheinen weiterhin konservativ' (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/redcare-pharmacy-aktie-springt-deutsche-bank-sieht-einstiegschance-q3-im-fokus). The DocMorris analogue: Octavian called its Q4-implied 8-9% guide cautious (https://www.boerse-online.de/dpa-afx/roundup-docmorris-waechst-dank-e-rezepten-kraeftig-und-erhoeht-jahresprognose-558541.html).

findings.finding: German non-Rx (OTC and beauty) was soft in Q3. Redcare itself flagged a 'softer July'. The closest peer, DocMorris, printed German non-Rx +5.5% and OTC only +3.5% for the same quarter, against Redcare's Q2 DACH non-Rx +12% and a FY group non-Rx guide of 10-12%. The release will carry the first Q3 non-Rx number, on the higher-margin ~57% of revenue, and it likely slows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Non-Rx slowing to 9.3% in Q4'25 was part of the FY25 release that fell -21.0% on 4 Mar 2026. The June 2026 raise, which leaned on a non-Rx re-acceleration (Germany 12% in April, 16% in May), brought +17.4%.
findings.original_quote: Deutlich geringer war das Wachstum im restlichen Geschäft in Deutschland (Non-Rx). Hier stieg der Umsatz um 5,5 Prozent auf 218 Millionen Franken. (Translation: growth in the rest of the German business, non-Rx, was markedly lower; revenue there rose 5.5% to CHF 218m.)
findings.why_not_priced: The DocMorris print was read as Rx-positive: Redcare rose about 3% in sympathy on 15 Oct and the coverage dwelt on Rx Germany +78%. The non-Rx softness drew no Redcare-specific comment I could find, and Redcare's own 28 Sep wording ('rebounded well in August and September') steers attention away from it. It is a peer proxy, not Redcare's number. Redcare's non-Rx Germany has outgrown DocMorris's before, and July is one month of three, so the finding is small.
findings.independence: Redcare's own pre-release admits the softer July: 'non-Rx revenue in Germany rebounded well in August and September after a softer July' (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/redcare-pharmacy-raises-full-year-2026-revenue-guidance-again-driven-by-strong-rx-momentum-in-germany/1ed5c44d-9182-480e-bc2c-a0e03c44f64c_en). German trade press: 'parallel dümpelt auch das Non-Rx-Geschäft mehr oder weniger kraftlos vor sich hin' (https://www.apotheke-adhoc.de/nachrichten/detail/markt/ceo-wechsel-welchen-weg-geht-redcare/).

findings.finding: This is the first quarterly report and call under CEO Peter Schmid von Linstow, appointed 14 Oct 2026. He is a platform and marketplace executive (Visable/Alibaba, Parship, eBay, AutoScout24), was on the supervisory board only since April, and has framed his agenda around AI and 'sustained, profitable growth'. A first call is where new priorities, investment or a re-based mid-term ambition (the company's standing target is an adj. EBITDA margin above 8%) would surface.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CEO-change announcement on 28 Aug 2026 brought -5.9% that day (gap +6.5% the day before was reversed).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has risen 8% since his 14 Oct start without any statement from him on targets, so the market is treating the transition as continuity. If a reset were priced, the run-up would have stalled into the print. The sign is genuinely unknown: a new CEO may also endorse the conservative guide. Hence a small negative from the base rate that new CEOs reset rather than raise.
findings.independence: German trade press asks in its headline 'CEO-Wechsel: Welchen Weg geht Redcare? OTC vs. Rx' (https://www.apotheke-adhoc.de/nachrichten/detail/markt/ceo-wechsel-welchen-weg-geht-redcare/, 2026-09-29), i.e. which way Redcare goes after the CEO change.

findings.finding: 2025 and 2026 are the company's declared 'peak investment years' (capex EUR 118.6m in 2025, on automation and capacity), and FY25 operating cash flow of EUR 31m came 'despite higher working capital requirements'. With Rx Germany growing about 56%, the 9M cash and working-capital line in the Q3 statement is a line the pre-release did not touch.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean instance on this name. The FY25 release that carried the peak-capex statement fell -21.0%, but on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody previews cash flow on this name; all coverage I found is on Rx growth and the guide. It is an inference from declared capex intensity and Rx working capital, with no Q3 cash number available, so it is small.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The sealed lean is +2.25 (mostly the short-squeeze component on a 4.28% disclosed short), and the conservative-guide finding agrees with it. The non-Rx, CEO and cash findings cut against it, and the 20d (+6.3%) and 60d (+21.8%) run-ups plus this name's habit of fading results-day gaps argue that a confirm-only release is sold. So the findings sum to about 0 and p_up stays at 50.
language_note: German trade press (apotheke adhoc, 29 Sep 2026) had a sceptical read of the second raise that the English wire did not: Venlo still expects a flattening curve, Q4 could be weaker than Q3, Rx money is going into the bonus/co-payment waiver, and non-Rx 'dümpelt kraftlos' (drifts along listlessly).
The DocMorris German non-Rx +5.5% / OTC +3.5% figure came from the German dpa-AFX roundup and retail-news.de; the English results I found carried only the Rx headline.
The Deutsche Bank 'Jahresziele konservativ' (targets look conservative) view and the 7 Oct Berenberg/MPCM target raises surfaced only in German retail portals (goldesel, finanztrends).
The company's own documents (EQS) are English-first and carried every hard number.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'you were too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 5.5 to 6.5, because a guidance change (a third raise, or a new-CEO reframing) is a live possibility on a 59%-vol name.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): added a small -0.3 cash/working-capital finding from the declared peak-capex years, a document already found in the hunt and not filed in the draft.
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': confirmed that the pre-released Rx Germany and margin lines stay in rejected_candidates as duplicates and not as findings.
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' plus this name's record of fading gaps: kept p_up at 50 and did not enlarge the guidance finding beyond +1.0.
